paragraphs: Friend, I know. That was a LOT of names. Tribe after tribe, family after family, and one tribe only got a single verse. But here's what I want you to hold onto: God's Word takes the time to write down real families, and the people on that list were real people (1 Chronicles 7:1-8:40).

And look at what the list keeps: the proud numbers, like Asher's men called "choice and mighty men of valor" (1 Chronicles 7:40), and the heartbreak. Ezer and Elead were killed by the men of Gath, and their father Ephraim "mourned for many days" (1 Chronicles 7:21-22). Then he named his next son Beriah, "because tragedy had come upon his house" (1 Chronicles 7:23). The Bible doesn't hide the hard parts of a family, and I think that's a comfort, because your story has some hard parts too.

So here's the big idea: God keeps the record of His people, the winners, the quiet ones and the hurting ones, and every one of them counts. I was stuck in the back of a junk drawer once, and I know what it feels like to wonder if anybody remembers your name. This chapter says the same thing the angel who called me out of that drawer said to me: you are not forgotten, so go bake like it, baker!
